chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about combining two surahs in the obligatory prayer and the supererogatory prayer. He said: There is no harm in it.

So the proper approach concerning this report is that we carry it upon a kind of concession, even though what we presented earlier is preferable, because combining two surahs is not among the things that invalidate the prayer. And the narrations have come explicitly indicating dislike.

key_terms.الرُّخْصَةِ: a concession or dispensation in the ruling
key_terms.السُّورَتَيْنِ: the two surahs being recited together
key_terms.الْأَفْضَلُ: that which is more virtuous or preferable
key_terms.الْقِرَانِ: joining or combining two surahs in one unit of prayer
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislike; a discouraged act that does not invalidate the prayer
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is reciting two surahs together in the obligatory prayer permissible in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on reciting two surahs together in salat (prayer), whether in the obligatory or supererogatory prayer. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no harm in it, while the compiler explains that this should be understood as a concession, since other narrations indicate that the practice is disliked though it does not invalidate the prayer.
